Get an increment of Over 10% | Business | Sarthak Ahuja

Why is the RBI saying that the inflation in India is double of what has been declared in the official numbers?

The RBI did a survey in March 2026 called the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households, by which the perceived inflation is at 7.2%...

When the Consumer Price Index (CPI) figure of inflation for Feb was reported to be 3.2%...

And as per the survey, people on the grounds expect inflation to be anywhere between 8.5% to 9% in the coming year...

So how can the inflation felt on ground be double of the reported numbers? Let’s look at all the factors...

👉🏻 First is the method of calculation of CPI has some major problems...

When they look at inflation in rent for example, which is the highest expense for most people, they look at all rented properties in India, where the annual escalation is just about 5-7%...

But for all the houses where a new tenant comes in, or the tenant changes, landlords increase rent by almost 15% or double digit percentages...

Sky News host Peta Credlin reacts to the RBA decision to hike interest rates to 4.35 per cent.

“As the Reserve Bank this afternoon increased the cash rate – up 25 basis points to 4.35 per cent – in part because the government can't stop spending, and its spending is fuelling inflation, Labor's got yet another handout on the way,” Ms Credlin said.
 
“The Australian reports today in a leak, the centrepiece of next week's budget, naturally dressed up as cost-of-living relief, will be a cash splash of up to $300 for every worker. 
 
“Presumably, that's what the PM means when he says that the budget would be ‘full of Labor values’.”
